public_rationale: Supported on the ordinary reading that broad failure categories persisted. The 1988 articles raise problems with systematic language processing and generalization. April 2022 research still documents compositional difficulties, semantic-understanding errors, hallucinations, and other unreliable outputs. The stronger reading that nothing relevant improved is not supported: PaLM's report records errors corrected by scaling, and Kirov and Cotterell report overcoming many specific Pinker–Prince objections. These improvements do not establish that the broad categories disappeared. This assessment does not endorse the rhetorical judgment 'inductive folly' or infer that neural approaches can never solve the remaining problems.
limitations: The outcome depends on interpreting 'have not changed' as persistence of categories.
The cited tests cover particular systems and tasks, not every neural architecture.
The evidence does not establish a common cause for old and modern failures.
The historical observation ends on May 14, 2022; subsequent capabilities are outside its scope.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Success on a few problems with a particular strategy in no way guarantees that all problems can be solved the same way, and it is inductive folly to think otherwise, especially as the failure modes (unreliability, bizarre errors, failures of compositionality and discomprehension) have not changed since Fodor and Pinker pointed them out in 1988.

statement.excerpt: Success on a few problems with a particular strategy in no way guarantees that we can solve all problems in a similar way. It is sheer inductive folly to imagine otherwise, particular when the failure modes (unreliability, bizarre errors, failures in compositionality and discomprehension) have not changed since Fodor and Pinker pointed them out (in separate articles) in 1988.

our_interpretation: The checkable historical assertion is that the broad kinds of failure identified in the 1988 critiques remained present in neural systems by May 14, 2022.
I read 'have not changed' as persistence of failure categories, rather than identical error rates, unchanged architectures, or no progress on individual problems.
I read compositionality as applying familiar components in unfamiliar combinations, and discomprehension as observable errors in interpreting meaning.
The target period follows the explicit comparison from 1988 through the post date. It does not extend to systems introduced after the post.

The statement about guarantees is a logical caution, and 'inductive folly' is an evaluative judgment. Neither is treated as a separate empirical forecast or as a prediction that neural methods can never succeed.
criteria.support_condition: The original critiques identify problems with systematic generalization and language processing, and research available by the post documents analogous compositional, comprehension, and unreliable or anomalous output failures in contemporary neural systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The original articles do not identify the relevant problems, or evidence establishes that the broad failure categories had been overcome by the post date. Improvements on particular tasks alone do not contradict persistence of the categories.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Part III, Systematicity of cognitive representation
evidence.publisher: Cognition; full-text copy hosted by the University of Waterloo
evidence.explanation: Fodor and Pylyshyn connect systematic understanding of related sentences to structured representations and challenge connectionist accounts on that basis. This establishes the historical comparison, not an empirical verdict on 2022 systems.

evidence.locator: Introductory list of shortcomings of the Rumelhart–McClelland model
evidence.publisher: Cognition; full-text reproduction hosted by Reinhard Blutner
evidence.explanation: Pinker and Prince document failures in a neural language-learning model, including missing outputs and faulty linguistic generalizations. Their task was past-tense learning, so connecting these failures to modern comprehension errors is a comparison of broad categories.

Tests involving SCAN and RobustFill found continuing difficulty combining learned components in new ways, even with modified Transformers. This supports persistence of compositional generalization problems while explicitly acknowledging progress.

evidence.locator: Section 6.3, Figure 9 and accompanying error analysis, page 20
evidence.publisher: arXiv; Aakanksha Chowdhery and colleagues, Google
evidence.explanation: The PaLM analysis identifies semantic-understanding errors, omitted reasoning steps, and anomalous outputs; Figure 9 shows that scaling corrected some but not all errors in each category. This supports persistent comprehension and reliability problems, while also providing evidence against unchanged error frequency.

evidence.locator: Section 6, Summary of Resolved and Outstanding Criticisms
evidence.publisher: arXiv; Christo Kirov and Ryan Cotterell
evidence.explanation: This direct revisit reports substantial improvements on the original past-tense problem and resolution of many specific objections. It challenges a literal claim of unchanged deficiencies, but does not establish elimination of the broad failure categories across neural AI.
